prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1345; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the claimant reporting a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection. The claimant reports neck and back strain and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy as a named driver and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. Statements from two independent witnesses and the other driver describe the collision in the same sequence as the claimant.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photos. The vehicle damage is largely consistent with the described impact speed and direction, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant by phone about the injury. The account matched the first notice of loss in every detail, and the reported neck and back strain is a plausible result of a collision of this type.

Entry 6: Claimant referred to a primary care provider for evaluation and started a standard course of physical therapy. Treatment notes show steady improvement and a gradual reduction in visits.

Entry 7: Checked prior claims and medical history. No earlier injury to the neck or back has been identified, and the claimant has not reported any other recent accidents.

Entry 8: Treatment has tapered off as the claimant has improved, consistent with the expected recovery timeline for this type of soft tissue injury. File remains open pending final medical update.
